messages:
Noah: Heads-up: noticed a cluster of tenants with invoice-preview spikes occurring exactly at the hour boundary. Final invoices are fine but previews show tokens assigned to the wrong hour bucket, which skews hourly graphs.

Ivy: Saw that too. This started after we flipped the ingest-watermarking change that moved from processing-time to event-time watermarking to reduce late-arrival reprocessing.

Sam: Are tokens actually miscounted or just bucketed into the previous hour?

Noah: Mostly mis-bucketed. Example: an event arrived at 12:01 with event_ts=11:59:58 due to client clock skew. Preview ingestion uses event_ts for grouping, but the preview chart assumes processing-time for display. So preview shows the token in 11:00-12:00 bucket while console hourly card uses server-time, causing confusion.

Rupesh: Billing pipeline canonicalizes by aligned invoice windows (daily UTC), so invoices don't change. This is purely preview UX/telemetry mismatch.

ClockBot: Telemetry scan -> ~2.3k events in last 24h with event_ts earlier than processing_ts by >30s. Top affected SDKs: js-sdk v3.1.1 and py-sdk v1.9.

Ivy: Two separate fixes: short term -> make preview charts use event-time when available and show an "event-time" badge. Longer term -> normalize event timestamps on ingest (apply small clamp +/- 2m) and emit clock-skew metric per tenant.

Sam: Risk of clamping is hiding real late arrivals. I prefer non-destructive normalization: add normalized_ts field used for preview grouping, leaving original event_ts intact. Also add a flag in console to toggle histogram mode (event-time vs processing-time).

Noah: Good call. UX should be explicit and reversible. Also we should surface a per-tenant clock-skew alert when >0.5% of events have skew >60s. That helps CS triage.

Rupesh: Backfill? If we change preview grouping we could re-run only the hourly previews for last 24h to correct charts. Cost small. Sam, can you estimate?

Sam: Reprocessing 24h previews for affected tenants ~1 CPU-hour and 200GB IO. I'll add a dry-run and surface top offenders before commit.

Billing: Add a note to billing dashboard: "Preview timeseries may use event timestamps and differ from processing-time displays during rollout." Also include a link to SDKs with clock-sync instructions.

ConsoleBot: Draft banner prepared. Approve before deploy?

Noah: Approve. Action items: Sam -> implement normalized_ts field + backfill job (dry-run), Ivy -> feature flag to toggle event-time charting and UI badge, Rupesh -> add clock-skew telemetry and alert, Noah -> post banner and coordinate SDK team for clock-sync guidance.

Ivy: I'll also add a small regression test that injects out-of-order event_ts and asserts charts display the badge and that normalized grouping happens under flag.

Sam: Opening PRs and job spec now, tagging @Ivy and @Rupesh.

Noah: Thanks team. Keeping thread open for backfill results.
